![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/f8d67ac4521b6b7fbe5027e1fef52ab5d44763e558aef13e970dbc72aa2636d9.png)

The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077122/assets/b696475163cf9627709e62d8315edca393afd46aa2dbff5f23b4583e20641864.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(-\frac{\pi }{2},0],$ we get the quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},0].
$$
